newsitem.title: GREECE: SFAKIANAKIS SAYS H1 SALES UP 21.8PCT, PRETAX FLAT.
newsitem.headline: SFAKIANAKIS SAYS H1 SALES UP 21.8PCT, PRETAX FLAT.

text.p: Greek automobile dealer Sfakianakis said in a statement its half-year sales grew 21.8 percent year-on-year to 21.01 billion drachmas, but pretax profit grew marginally to 2.73 billion drachmas from 2.71 billion.

The discrepancy between sales and pretax profit was mainly attributed to a 0.7 billion drachma increase in general and distribution expenses along with a 0.57 billion drachma drop in other operating income, financial officer Manolis Lekakis told Reuters.
"The improvement in financial expenses only partially offset higher expense items," he said.
But 1997 results would meet earlier company projections for pretax earnings of 4.1 billion drachmas and gross profit of 6.65 billion on turnover of 32.5 billion drachmas.
"Our 1997 results will be in line with our estimates stated in the IPO prospectus and may well turn out slightly better," Lekakis said.
In 1996, pretax earnings rose 58 percent to 3.78 billion drachmas on turnover growth of 31 percent to 32.7 billion.
Over the first half, gross profit was up 29.8 percent to 4.82 billion drachmas against 3.71 billion a year earlier, the company said.
Sfakianakis which sells mostly Suzuki vehicles is Greece's most profitable auto dealer. It ranked 39th amongst Greece's commercial companies in terms of sales -- 8th based on pretax profit.
Auto sales between January and June 1997 were up 21.3 percent to 5,244 units over the respective period of 1996, with its market share advancing to 6.4 from 5.2 percent, the company said.
Sales of motorcycles were up 15.9 percent in the first half to 2,086 units, Sfakianakis' market share rising to 7.55 percent from year-earlier 4.99 percent, it said.
The company said it revised upwards the prospectus' target for the sale of 8,000 cars and 3,500 motorcycles in 1997 to 8,600 cars and 3,800 motorcycles.
Sfakianakis was listed on the Athens bourse's main market on June 18 after tapping the capital market for 4.25 billion drachmas in late May 1997.
The IPO was subscribed 7.38 times with the tranche allocated to institutional and retail investors being subscribed 9.5 and 6.4 times respectively.

Sfakianakis' shares closed at 1,750 drachmas on Wednesday, a nadir since their June 18 listing at 2,000 drachmas, but were up 15 drachmas around Thursday's mid-session. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
